title: Model/runtime deprecation & rollout tooling for graceful upgrades and fallbacks
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Add a unified deprecation + rollout framework that ensures model/runtime pairings remain compatible across pinned and floating deployments. Deliverables: API for declaring compatibility ranges per model artifact, routing rules that prefer pinned pairings but allow safe automatic fallback to the nearest compatible runtime or model variant, console rollout gate UI, and a migration helper CLI that computes impact and recommends canary percentages.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility table stored in metadata service and queryable by routing layer
Router honors pin + fallback precedence: strict pin -> pinned model runtime variants -> compatibility-compatible model-runtime pairs -> global fallback model variant
Console shows rollout gate with automatic rollback on error rate or regression to quality metric thresholds
Migration CLI produces a deterministic plan with estimated QPS impact and token-cost delta

End-to-end integration tests covering: 1) pinned customer using older runtime, 2) floating customer receiving safe fallback when pinned backend unavailable, 3) canary rollout detects degraded output quality and triggers rollback
technical_decisions: Use semver-ish range expressions on runtime versions (major.minor) and store compatibility as string ranges in metadata service
Compatibility resolution performed in router: prefer exact model+runtime pin stored on customer resource, then attempt model-family compatible runtime, then fallback to pre-approved global variant
Rollout gates are implemented as composable predicates: latency_percentile, error_rate, eval_set_regression. Thresholds are configurable per release channel.
Migration tool will be read-only by default; apply mode will create canary routes via existing routing APIs instead of mutating customer configs directly
work_items: Add compatibility schema to metadata service and migration import script
Router: implement compatibility resolver and unit tests
Console: rollout gate UI + rollout plan preview
CLI: migration dry-run and apply modes, output as JSON and human-readable plan
E2E test harness: synthetic workload with quality eval hooks
Update runbook with rollback steps and incident playbook
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created. Initial scope drafted after post-mortem on spillover incident where new runtime caused unseen semi-silent quality regressions.
2026-02-25: Spike complete. Validated storing compatibility as range strings is performant at 10k qps with in-memory cache. Chose router-side resolution to avoid cross-service latencies.
2026-03-03: Prototype router resolver merged behind feature flag. Early bench: decision latency +0.6ms median under typical load.
2026-03-08: Console rollout gate mockups reviewed by PM and Design; minor UX changes requested to emphasize rollback actionability.
2026-03-10: Began migration CLI implementation; dry-run prints expected canary percentages and token-cost delta for sample customers
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect compatibility mappings could route traffic to incompatible runtimes leading to silent corruption. Mitigation: require a signed compatibility artifact and two-phase import with validation harness.
Risk: Rollout gate thresholds too strict prevent needed migrations. Mitigation: provide preview mode and a manual override with audit trail.

Risk: Performance overhead in router. Mitigation: cache resolution results keyed by model-version + customer pin and evict on metadata change; fall back to stale result for 200ms if metadata store slow
